name: TESTOSTERONE TOTAL
description: Total Testosterone measures the primary male sex hormone using chemiluminescent immunoassay. This test evaluates androgen status in men and women, helping diagnose hypogonadism, infertility, hirsutism, and other hormonal disorders. Testosterone exists in free and protein-bound forms.

testdetails.instrumentation: Abbott Architect, Roche Elecsys, Beckman Coulter

literatureReview: Testosterone is the primary androgen hormone essential for male development, sexual function, muscle mass, and bone health. Total testosterone includes free and protein-bound fractions. The test uses competitive chemiluminescent immunoassays with high sensitivity. Adult male reference range is 300-1000 ng/dL, female range is 15-70 ng/dL. Low testosterone (hypogonadism) causes fatigue, reduced libido, erectile dysfunction, and loss of muscle mass. High levels in women can cause hirsutism and virilization. Morning sampling is preferred due to diurnal variation. Sex hormone binding globulin (SHBG) levels help interpret total testosterone. Free testosterone measurement may be needed in certain cases. Results should be interpreted with clinical symptoms and may require repeat testing.
